findings: Anteroposterior (AP) projection of the forearm demonstrating the radius and ulna with partial visualization of the wrist (distal) and elbow (proximal) joints

The medullary cavities of both the radius and ulna show markedly increased trabecular density with a coarse, 'cottonwool' or granular pattern replacing the normal fatty marrow signal throughout the diaphyses and metaphyses
The cortices of both bones appear thickened and expanded, with loss of the normal distinct corticomedullary differentiation
No discrete fracture line is identified
No periosteal reaction or aggressive cortical destruction is seen
Soft tissues appear mildly enlarged/prominent on the medial (ulnar) aspect of the forearm
Open physes are visible at both the distal radius/ulna and proximally, consistent with a skeletally immature individual
The trabecular pattern is diffusely abnormal bilaterally, affecting the entire visible length of both bones
differential: Osteopetrosis (marble bone disease): diffuse symmetric medullary sclerosis obliterating marrow space, cortical thickening, and lack of normal corticomedullary differentiation are classic features
Paget disease (polyostotic, though unusual in this age group): coarsened trabecular pattern with cortical thickening; however, typical bowing and flame-shaped lytic fronts are absent

Myelofibrosis or hematologic disorder causing diffuse medullary sclerosis (e.g., sickle cell disease with infarction, mastocytosis): diffuse increased medullary density bilaterally, though usually less homogeneous
anatomyConcerns: Open growth plates suggest a skeletally immature subject, which is atypical for Paget disease and makes that diagnosis less likely
Only a single projection (AP) is provided; a lateral view would be required for complete assessment
Proximal extent of the image is cropped, limiting full evaluation of the elbow joint
